I'm 60 years old and I've been farming these fields in Quzhou for over 40 years. Finished middle school, so I can read fertilizer labels and mostly understand what the extension people say, though I still trust my own eyes and what my neighbors do more than any book. My son works in Shijiazhuang now, so it's just me and my wife handling the land — about 8 mu all together.

I've got winter wheat in the ground already, planted last October. I'll stick with wheat and maize this year, same as always. I thought about cotton like some folks in the southern villages, but at my age I don't have the back for all that picking and spraying. Wheat-maize double cropping is hard work too, but at least I know it, and the machinery guys help with harvest.

For the wheat, I used improved seed — not some fancy new thing, just the good improved variety that Old Wang down the lane recommended, the one that resisted disease well last year. I rotary-tilled before planting, like I always do. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, and I'll topdress with urea at jointing now in spring. All told that's about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, maybe 6 kg of phosphorus and 5 kg of potassium. The extension fellow says 15 kg nitrogen is enough, but I've seen too many yellow fields in May, so I put a little extra. Better to waste a few yuan than lose a whole crop.

I'll irrigate four times for the wheat — already did the winter water and the green-up water in March. Now I need to water at jointing in April, and once more at grain filling in May. Water costs money but wheat is thirsty. I'll spray herbicide once in spring, and if I see aphids I'll spray insecticide once or twice. Three pesticide applications total should do it.

After wheat harvest in early June, I'll plant summer maize straight away — no time to plough, everyone uses no-tillage now, just drill the seed right into the wheat stubble. I'll use hybrid maize seed, the kind that gives good yield even with a short season. Fertilizer will be about 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, 4 kg potassium per mu. I'll irrigate twice if the summer rains are patchy. Herbicide at planting and a couple of insecticide sprays for the borers. 

If the weather is normal, I expect about 480 kg per mu from the wheat and 550 kg per mu from the maize. That's what I usually get, and what my neighbors get. I'm not trying to break records — I just need steady income and enough to eat.
